sentences.text: This pterosaur lived in the Crato Formation of Brazil and lacked a snout crest but had one at the back of its skull.
Its skull measured over 66 centimeters long, and scientists estimate the wingspan reached four meters.
The name means 'playful finger' because it mixed a Latin word for play with a Greek word for finger.
A yucca leaf stuck in its jaw suggests the creature caught the plant, failed to remove it, and likely died from starvation.
Eberhard Frey and colleagues named the genus in 2003, creating the single species L. sibbicki.
A 2014 analysis by Brian Andres and colleagues placed it as a derived member of Anhangueria, linking it to ornithocheirids and anhanguerids.
Earlier work by Andres and Myers in 2013 showed it was more closely related to those groups than to Brasileodactylus.
The animal lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
In 2007, Frey suggested the name might be a junior synonym of Brasileodactylus, though later studies disagreed with this view.
